scope: Post-primary exploratory baseline-proxy audit; prior G-agreement results were already known when this question was selected
question: Does omitting the held-native future velocity change materially affect the actual I56 current-velocity-plus-differential-G objective proxy, even when paired G is accurate?
sources: Only already-sealed I57 held-native/governed endpoint arrays, root registration, and exact frozen model matrices/predictions
frames: Endpoint angular qvel is rotated separately into world; transverse angular velocity is then represented in the common initial fork frame. Planar velocity remains in world XY and yaw is physical world-Z angular velocity.
comparisons: Actual held native versus current velocity (the native center of the current-plus-G-delta proxy)
Actual held governed versus current velocity plus G_h times (u_governed-u_native)
Actual held native and governed versus their exact frozen affine offset+G_h u
Governed proxy error equals omitted native baseline drift plus paired differential prediction error
Governed affine error equals native affine error plus paired differential prediction error
outputs: Retain every 10-component physical/common-frame value and planar/transverse/yaw/encoder group vectors, signed errors, norms and decomposition residuals. Include both model horizons and both events.
decision_boundary: Descriptive exploratory arithmetic only. No fitting, retuning, new physics, new acceptance gates, controller adoption, or attribution of the entire trajectory deviation. Affine offsets remain unvalidated soft-contact approximations.
